[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Per a North Dakota governors office press release, this is an Atlas Power data center complex under construction on a 77 acre site west of Williston, North Dakota, a roughly 1.9 billion dollar multiyear investment built by FX Solutions Inc and powered by Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative. Planned capacity is staged: Phase 1 totals 240 MW across 16 buildings (350 by 30 feet each), Phase 2 expands to 500 MW, and Phase 3 to 700 MW. The release quotes Atlas Power founder and president Kevin Washington describing this as set to become the companys largest center of operations, building on an existing Atlas Power site in Butte, Montana. These figures describe planned and under construction capacity, not yet operating capacity, and critical_it_mw is left unset here rather than populated with a construction phase target.

planned_phases.detail: 16 buildings, each 350 feet by 30 feet, housing tens of thousands of servers

profile.planned_capacity: Phase 1: 240 MW across 16 buildings; Phase 2: expansion to 500 MW; Phase 3: expansion to 700 MW (all planned/under construction, not yet operating)

compliance_history.event: Williams County began receiving noise complaints from residents around the site; county staff identified building code and zoning ordinance violations while responding, and determined that eight Phase 2 buildings were operating without the required Certificate of Occupancy.
The Board of County Commissioners gave Atlas Power 45 days to rectify the identified violations.

Told the May order had not been fully addressed, the Board directed Mountrail-Williams Electric Cooperative to disconnect power to buildings on the Phase 2 permit, under the authority of the county building code.
MWEC served a Petition for Declaratory Judgment on the county and did not comply with the disconnection directive.

The Board unanimously approved a standard 60-day Temporary Certificate of Occupancy after officials confirmed the code violations were rectified, state and county inspection requirements met, and $232,000 in fines paid. A full Certificate of Occupancy was to be considered after acoustical panels, security fencing and a required emergency access road were completed.

reading.body:
The Atlas Power Williston Datacenter was announced in January 2022 with a three-phase buildout targeting 700 MW at full build, on a 77-acre site in Williams County, North Dakota, backed by a stated $1.9 billion investment. That 700 MW figure is a Phase 3 target from the announcement, not a verified operating figure, and no operator-published number for energized capacity exists. This site deliberately excludes it from the state capacity total for that reason. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 700 MW of IT load would be roughly 17,500 racks, and Phase 1 alone, at 240 MW across 16 buildings, would be roughly 6,000 racks on the same assumption, but neither figure is the operator's claim and neither can be confirmed against actual operating load.

The compliance record is material to any assessment of operating status. Eight Phase 2 buildings were found to be running without Certificates of Occupancy as of April 2023, county commissioners ordered rectification in May, the power cooperative was directed to disconnect those buildings in June after the order went unmet, and the cooperative itself responded by filing for declaratory judgment rather than complying. A 60-day Temporary Certificate of Occupancy was granted on June 29, 2023, after violations were resolved, inspections passed, and $232,000 in fines paid. Whether a full Certificate of Occupancy was subsequently issued is not published in the sources held here. The stated workload is high-density computing and cryptocurrency mining, which describes what the campus was designed to host but does not confirm AI training tenancy.

North Dakota has three data center facilities mapped in this site's dataset, none of which have a verified operator-published megawatt figure, giving the state a published capacity total of zero megawatts by this site's methodology. Atlas Power Williston ranks first among those three facilities by published MW only in the sense that all three are tied at unpublished, and the announced ceiling is the largest number associated with any of them. The state context makes clear that North Dakota is poorly represented in primary-source capacity data, and this campus, despite its scale on paper, contributes nothing verifiable to that picture until operating figures are confirmed from the operator directly.
